purpose: Designed identification probes for NAM -> GP50 CLO system identification/distillation.
notes: All files are mono float32 WAV.
44.1 kHz is the canonical domain because the GP50 CLO student is ultimately 44.1 kHz.
If the NAM requires another sample rate, resample the input to the NAM rate, render the NAM, then resample/alignment-correct the target back to 44.1 kHz before fitting.
Do not normalise the NAM output independently; preserve absolute input/output gain.
Use a deterministic high-quality resampler and cache teacher renders.

files.description: Two seconds of digital silence. Useful for state reset / noise-floor / latency sanity checks.
Single positive impulse at -36 dBFS after 0.5 s silence. Low-level linear-response / latency probe.
Single positive impulse at -12 dBFS after 0.5 s silence. Low-level linear-response / latency probe.
Matched positive/negative 4 ms pulses at -30, -18, -9 and -3 dBFS. Exposes polarity asymmetry and transient saturation.
20 Hz -> 20 kHz logarithmic sweep, peak -36 dBFS. Compare low/mid/high-drive spectral behaviour.
20 Hz -> 20 kHz logarithmic sweep, peak -18 dBFS. Compare low/mid/high-drive spectral behaviour.
20 Hz -> 20 kHz logarithmic sweep, peak -6 dBFS. Compare low/mid/high-drive spectral behaviour.
Identical 23-tone multisine repeated from -36 to -3 dBFS peak. Designed for level-dependent gain, tone and compression measurements.
23-tone multisine with smooth peak-drive envelope from -36 dBFS to -3 dBFS and back. Useful for compression onset, cleanup and hysteresis/state checks.
1 kHz sine at absolute peak levels -42 to -1 dBFS. Measures transfer curve, compression and harmonic growth.
100/400/1000/2500/5000 Hz sines at -30/-18/-9/-3 dBFS. Exposes frequency-dependent nonlinear behaviour.
Two-tone pairs at three levels for intermodulation behaviour: 100+1000, 250+2000, 500+4000, 1000+5000 Hz.
Identical deterministic broadband noise repeated at multiple peak levels. Useful for broad transfer estimation and level-dependent response.
Short tone bursts from 80 Hz to 4 kHz at -18/-6/-3 dBFS. Tests attack/release behaviour and transient distortion.
Sparse decaying broadband transients at varied levels. Synthetic transient probe only; do not treat as a substitute for real guitar DI.
